clue.text: A thorough proficient in getting over turbulent stream

indicators.note: turbulent water is churned up, so the letters of the following word are tossed into a new order

parts.note: getting over something means putting it past you; past = over
the six letters of stream rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone skilled at crossing rough water, such as a river guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A past master is an expert of long practice, someone thoroughly proficient at a skill.

clue.text: Quietly bolt into the shrub

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for quietly
a rivet is a metal bolt

explanation.surface: Slipping silently into a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolt suggests running off, but it is the fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: Privet is an evergreen shrub widely grown for hedges.

clue.text: Animals brought up by celebrity

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means raised from bottom to top, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: rats are animals; the general word stands for a specific example

explanation.surface: Pets raised by a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer, so the word stands for a celebrity.

clue.text: I'm improving morale — is this a record?

indicators.note: improving means reworking into a better form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boosting team spirit wonders if they have set a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorial is something that preserves memory, such as a written record or monument.

clue.text: Paid for the ware ordered for fine spell

indicators.note: ordered means put in a fresh sequence, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a bill settled has been paid
seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Settling the bill for goods that were ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordered reads as goods sent for, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period of weather; settled weather is a stretch of dry, calm conditions.

clue.text: Essential part of earth for example

definitions.meaning: second meaning: earth was one of the four classical ... with air, fire and water

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the core of the planet; earth is instead one of the ancient four.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a fundamental component, and in old natural philosophy earth was one of four basic substances.

clue.text: Never upset about oriental superficial show

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
E for east, as oriental means eastern

explanation.surface: A grumble that an Eastern display was only skin-deep.
explanation.walkthrough: The E is not neatly inserted anywhere: the five letters of never plus E are simply rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin decorative facing, and figuratively an outward appearance that hides what lies beneath.

clue.text: Journalist, sorely tried in love …

indicators.note: sorely suggests something painfully wrenched, so the word that follows is jumbled
in places the reworked letters around the zero

parts.note: the five letters rearranged
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A reporter put through heartache by a romance, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue's story to the next one; the two are solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a newspaper journalist who prepares and oversees what is published.

clue.text: … yet a cruel upset for Australian grower

indicators.note: upset means overturned and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: all fourteen letters, the signal word included

explanation.surface: The heartbroken reporter's story goes on: yet another cruel blow.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset does double duty: it signals the rearrangement and also supplies its own letters to the fourteen.
explanation.definitionFit: The gum tree is native to Australia, and anything growing there can be called a grower.

clue.text: Having owned up, allowed to enter

explanation.surface: A person who confessed and was then let into somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle covers both confessing to something and being granted entry through a door.

clue.text: Find record surplus

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
surplus means left over

explanation.surface: Turning up an unusually large supply of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something is to come upon it, which is a plain synonym of discover.

clue.text: Wave that may be seen in a lady's hair

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long heavy sea wave that rolls in

definitions.text: that may be seen in a lady's hair
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a curler used to set hair

explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes wave a hairstyle, but the first meaning is the sea's kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a big breaking sea wave and also the cylinder a woman wraps hair around to curl it.

clue.text: Examines and compares late passes out

indicators.note: the passes sit outside, wrapping round the word before them

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
taken as written

explanation.surface: An official checking tardy permits handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'passes out' as one phrase and the clue seems about fainting; out goes with passes to put them around late.
explanation.definitionFit: To collate is to gather texts and check them against each other, examining and comparing them.

clue.text: Good fellow for plant variant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a decent, obliging person
second meaning: a botanical mutation differing from its parent

explanation.walkthrough: Good fellow is chiefly British and Australian usage, as in 'be a good sport'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport is a cheerful, generous person, and in botany a shoot or plant that mutates from the normal type.

clue.text: Praises for archbishop in mine's

indicators.note: in places the archbishop inside the mines

parts.note: a pit is a mine; mine's read as mines
William Laud, Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

explanation.surface: Tributes paid to a churchman by a mining community.
explanation.walkthrough: Laud is also a verb meaning praise, so the archbishop doubles the definition's hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaudits are expressions of applause and approval, the plural noun matching praises.

clue.text: Produce article about first nuclear instrument

indicators.note: to produce is to make something new out of material, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'first' keeps only the first letter of 'nuclear'

parts.note: the first letter of nuclear

explanation.surface: A writer turning out a piece on early atomic equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Article tempts the solver to think of a or the, but here it is used in full.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a single-reed woodwind musical instrument.

clue.text: Rebel forced to rely on power unit

indicators.note: something forced is wrenched out of shape, so the letters are pushed into another order

parts.note: the watt is the SI unit of power
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An insurgent compelled to depend on a generator.
explanation.walkthrough: On means the rearranged letters come after the power unit. Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat Tyler is the best-known leader of the 1381 English uprising, a historical rebel.

clue.text: Shell for the solitary sail or?

parts.note: run together it is sailor, and AB is an able seaman
solitary means alone

explanation.surface: Asking whether a lone yachtsman should take a hull or a sail.
explanation.walkthrough: The split sail or must be joined to read sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is a sea snail whose shell is lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Music in stock

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a passage of melody

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a shop's inventory of records.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a snatch of melody and also a line of descent, as in a strain of a breed.

clue.text: Celebration over treaty drafted in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: in puts the reworked word inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: the six letters rearranged

indicators.note: a draft is a rough version written out anew, so the letters are set down in fresh order

parts.note: PA is the US postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A party thrown after an agreement is written up in Philadelphia.
explanation.walkthrough: The American setting nods to the Boston Tea Party, though that was Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is a social gathering, a modest kind of celebration.

clue.text: Nag perhaps on going to eat out with a relation of father's?

indicators.note: perhaps means the word is only one possible form, so its letters may come in another order
out means disordered, so the second word is rearranged too

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse taken out to dinner along with someone's father's kin.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnate is a kinsman descended through the male line, a relative on the father's side.

clue.text: Lady was taken in perhaps by cable

indicators.note: perhaps means the word is only one possible arrangement, so its letters may be shuffled
taken in means held inside by the lady

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a lady
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman deceived by a telegram.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken in and cable both suggest a woman fooled by a telegram; here cable is a ship's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or cable used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: Bird taken to church by manservant

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
CH is the standard abbreviation for church
the first half of this word, man, is taken as written; its second half is the definition

explanation.surface: A manservant carrying a chicken to church.
explanation.walkthrough: Manservant looks like a single word but splits: man is wordplay and servant the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A henchman is a faithful follower or attendant, a servant who does a master's bidding.

clue.text: Plant the lady's bed first

parts.note: her is the possessive for the lady

indicators.note: first picks only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: opening letter of bed

explanation.surface: Setting out a woman's flowerbed before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: First looks like an instruction to put the bed in front, but it keeps only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb is any small seed-bearing plant without a woody stem.

clue.text: Sea-robin treated and smoked in assembly?

indicators.note: something treated is processed and changed, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the fish's name taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A gurnard cured and smoked for a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is two-faced: Sobranie was a well-known brand of cigarettes, and the Sobranie is Bulgaria's parliament, an assembly. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobranie names both a smoked cigarette brand and the Bulgarian national assembly, so it is smoked and an assembly.

clue.text: Try to force worker to follow oppressive ruler

indicators.note: forcing something bends it out of its shape, so the letters are wrenched about

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
a worker ant; worker is a common crossword cue for ant

explanation.surface: A despot trying to coerce a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: To follow puts the worker after the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel and oppressive ruler, the classic example of one.

clue.text: Delightful way of conducting cell debate

indicators.note: a way of conducting means a manner of handling or arranging, so the letters are organised afresh

parts.note: ten letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A pleasant method of running a discussion among prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable means highly pleasing, especially to taste, a close synonym for delightful.
